findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)). A team admin who is not also an owner will be rejected, and depending on isTeamAdmin's role semantics even owners may be rejected. The new UI action then fails with you_do_not_have_permission for intended team administrators. Use an OR/combined membership check.

findings.title: Any attendee can add guests to a booking
findings.body: The same guard also treats any attendee as authorized (isAttendee). The mutation only needs a bookingId and the caller's session, so any booker/guest on a booking can add arbitrary addresses to it, which then triggers calendar updates and emails to every attendee. The new UI is host-facing and does not expose attendee self-service, so this is an unintended write/notification path unless explicitly required.

findings.title: Guest filtering does not deduplicate or normalize email addresses
findings.body: uniqueGuests compares each submitted email against existing attendees and the blacklist, but never deduplicates the submitted array or normalizes case. A direct tRPC call with duplicate addresses can insert duplicate attendee rows (or hit a unique constraint) and send duplicate invites, and an uppercase variant of an existing or blacklisted address bypasses both checks because BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased but guest is not. Normalize/trim/lowercase and dedupe with a Set before writing.

findings.title: No booking status check before adding guests
findings.body: The handler never checks booking.status. A caller with permission can add guests to a cancelled or rejected booking, which then writes attendee rows and attempts calendar/email updates for an event that is no longer active. Reject non-active statuses before the update.

findings.title: Event manager uses the caller's credentials, not the booking owner's
findings.body: booking.user.credentials are loaded by the query but are not used; EventManager is constructed with getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). For a team admin/owner or attendee modifying another host's booking, the calendar operation therefore runs with the caller's credentials instead of the booking owner's, so the organizer's calendar event may not be updated or the wrong calendar may be touched. Use the booking owner's credentials/identity for the event manager.

findings.title: Attendee rows are committed before the calendar update
findings.body: The prisma.booking.update creates attendee rows before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees and before email dispatch. If the calendar update throws, the booking keeps the new attendees but the calendar was not updated; retrying the same guests is then rejected because uniqueGuests sees them as existing. Move the calendar work before the DB write or add rollback/recovery handling.

findings.title: Add-guests emails ignore event-type disableStandardEmails settings
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails sends organizer/team and attendee emails unconditionally. Other send helpers in this file accept eventTypeMetadata and honor disableStandardEmails for host/attendee. The handler has booking.eventType loaded and can pass metadata, but it does not, so event types configured to suppress standard emails will still email everyone when a guest is added.

findings.title: Hidden calendar notes can leak in add-guests emails
findings.body: When hideCalendarNotes is true, sendScheduledEmails removes additionalNotes before constructing attendee emails. sendAddGuestsEmails does not do this; it passes the full calendarEvent to AttendeeScheduledEmail/AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. A new guest can therefore receive notes that the event type is configured to hide from attendees.

findings.title: Email dispatch receives raw guests instead of filtered uniqueGuests
findings.body: addGuestsHandler calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the raw request array rather than uniqueGuests. sendAddGuestsEmails treats every email in newGuests as newly added and sends the full scheduled email to matching attendees. If the request included an existing attendee along with at least one valid new guest, that existing attendee is misclassified and receives a scheduled email instead of the add-guests notification. Pass the filtered uniqueGuests.

findings.title: Invalid-email state is not reset on success or close
findings.body: onSuccess resets multiEmailValue but not isInvalidEmail, and closing the dialog through onOpenChange also leaves it set. After one validation error, correcting the input and succeeding leaves isInvalidEmail true, so reopening the dialog immediately shows 'Emails must be unique and valid' even though the field is empty. Reset both state values on success and on close.

findings.title: Error toast fallback is unreachable
findings.body: The expression `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` always produces a non-empty string, so `message || t('unable_to_add_guests')` can never fall back. If err.data is absent users see a message beginning with 'undefined:'. Build the message with an explicit fallback when the code/translation is missing.

findings.title: No tests cover the new addGuests mutation
findings.body: No tests are added for the new addGuests mutation. It changes authorization (organizer/team admin/attendee), duplicate and blacklist filtering, booking status handling, calendar integration, and email recipient selection. Those paths are security/data-integrity sensitive and should be covered by tests to prevent regressions.
